newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Mosel chip plant sets June start.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Mosel chip plant sets June start.

text.p: Taiwan's Mosel Vitelic said on Wednesday it had completed testing of an advanced US$1.7 billion memory chip venture with German electronics giant Siemens AG and would put the plant into production in June.

Mosel, which holds a 62 percent stake in the Taiwan-based venture, said the plant would have initial monthly capacity of 5,000 64-megabit dynamic random access memory chips, getting an early start in the competitive high-capacity chip market.
"Our products can be launched at the same time that major makers in Japan and (South) Korea also launch their 64-megabit DRAMs," Mosel said in a statement.
"This should largely narrow the generation gap between our memory products and those in Japan and Korea."
Mosel has said capacity would reach 20,000 eight-inch wafers of DRAMs in 1997 and 40,000 wafers by the end of 1998 and that the venture eventually would expand to make 256-megabit DRAMs.
The joint venture, ProMOS Technologies Inc, has been set up in northern Taiwan's Hsinchu science park, outside Taipei.
Mosel, which listed shares on Taiwan's main stock market in 1995, is one of the island's leading DRAM makers.
